dynamic.architecture_summary: Single-process Flask application exposing a REST API for order management. Domain logic is encapsulated in dataclass-based models and an in-memory OrderStore, while src/app.py defines the HTTP routing layer. The architecture is intentionally minimal with no database; the store is swappable for a persistent backend.

key_components.name: App (Flask routes)
key_components.responsibility: Defines all HTTP endpoints for order CRUD operations and wires requests to the OrderStore.

key_components.name: Models
key_components.responsibility: Contains the Order dataclass and the OrderStore in-memory repository.

key_components.name: Tests
key_components.responsibility: Test suite covering the order API endpoints.

agent_safe_operations: Adding new fields to the Order dataclass in src/models.py (with defaults for backward compatibility)
Adding new test cases in tests/test_orders.py
Adding new model classes in src/models.py
Refactoring OrderStore internals without changing its public interface
agent_forbidden_operations: Removing or renaming existing public API endpoints without updating all callers and tests
Changing the Order.to_dict() keys as external consumers depend on that schema
Replacing the in-memory store with a database dependency without adding corresponding setup/migration logic
Modifying the module-level `store` singleton pattern in app.py in a way that breaks test isolation
potential_pitfalls: The OrderStore is a module-level singleton in app.py; state leaks between tests unless each test creates a fresh Flask test client or resets the store.
Order IDs are random UUIDs, so tests must capture the ID from the creation response rather than hardcoding values.
The app uses abort() which returns HTML error pages by default, not JSON; custom error handlers may be needed for consistent API responses.
Order.created_at is set at instantiation time via default_factory, making time-dependent assertions fragile without mocking datetime.
items is typed as list[dict[str, Any]] with no validation beyond non-emptiness; adding schema validation later could break existing tests.
